AbstractText.Label: Background
AbstractText.content: Family-centered care for preterm infants in Western societies has yielded short- to medium-term benefits. However, the intervention effects have rarely been validated in Eastern societies.

AbstractText.Label: Objective
AbstractText.content: The aim of this study was to examine whether a family-centered intervention program (FCIP) could improve the short-term medical and neurobehavioral outcomes in preterm infants with very low birth weight (VLBW; a birth weight of <1,500 g) in Taiwan over the outcomes seen with a usual care program (UCP).

AbstractText.Label: Design
AbstractText.content: This was a multicenter, single-blind, randomized controlled trial study.

AbstractText.Label: Setting
AbstractText.content: Three medical centers in northern and southern Taiwan were the locations for the study.

AbstractText.Label: Participants
AbstractText.content: The participants were 251 VLBW preterm infants without severe perinatal complications.

AbstractText.Label: Intervention
AbstractText.content: The infants were randomly assigned to receive the FCIP or the UCP during hospitalization.

AbstractText.Label: Measurements
AbstractText.content: Infant morbidities, feeding, growth, and neurobehavioral performance were evaluated during the neonatal period. Parental adherence to interventions was measured in the FCIP group.

AbstractText.Label: Results
AbstractText.content: The FCIP promoted earlier full enteral feeding (β = -1.1 weeks; 95% CI = -1.9 to -0.2 weeks) and hospital discharge (β = -0.6 week; 95% CI = -1.1 to -0.1 weeks), greater weight gain (β = 3.3 g/d; 95% CI = 0.1 to 6.6 g/d), and better neurobehavioral performance than the UCP (β = 1.2 points; 95% CI = 0.2 to 2.3 points). Furthermore, a higher degree of parental motivation in interventions, goal attainment, and comprehensiveness of home activities was significantly associated with greater effects in infants' neurobehavioral performance and weight gain (r = .20-.31; all Ps < .05).

AbstractText.Label: Limitations
AbstractText.content: The findings may not be generalized to preterm infants with severe perinatal diseases and parents with a low level of interest in interventions.

AbstractText.Label: Conclusions
AbstractText.content: Family-centered care facilitated short-term medical and neurobehavioral outcomes in VLBW preterm infants in Taiwan; the effects were likely achieved through parental adherence to interventions. The designated strategies may be considered in a future launch of family-centered care in Taiwan.
